independent_computation.step_1_scenario_reading: The scenario id 'syndra_custom_order_60' = Syndra + an explicit (non-default) cast_order + the champion's 'splinters' option set to 60. 60 is one of Syndra's own sourced Splinter-of-Wrath thresholds (40 Q charges / 60 W true damage / 80 E / 100 R / 120 AP), and the audit row confirms the module exposes exactly that option. 60 >= 40, so Dark Sphere is charge-stocked in this scenario (up to 2 stocked casts).

step_2_sourced_cast_times.note: castTime 'none' means the cast occupies no time on the shared timeline; E and R are the only Syndra casts with a nonzero sourced cast time, both 0.25 s.

independent_computation.step_3_scheduling_rule: Per math-foundations 1.1, cast epoch(k) = sum of the cast times of casts 0..k-1, pushed later only if the ability being cast is still on cooldown. Consequence: every legal Syndra cast epoch is an integer multiple of 0.25 s, and the earliest epoch for cast index 4 in an opening containing exactly one 0.25 s cast (E or R) is 0 + 0 + 0 + 0.25 = 0.25 s.
independent_computation.step_4_is_0_25_legal: Syndra has four castable slots, so a 5-cast opening must repeat one slot. The only Syndra slot that repeats without waiting on a cooldown is Dark Sphere, because at >= 40 Splinters it stocks charges ('up to a maximum of 2') and a stocked charge is spent immediately (corroborated by the ammo atom, which names Syndra's Dark Sphere as a stocked-cast resource). A custom cast order is exactly the mechanism needed to spend that second charge, since DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER is a flat Q,W,E,R. Hence a fifth cast at t = 0.25 s is legal and is the earliest epoch the model permits.

step_5_can_5_0_be_derived.as_cast_time_prefix_sum: No. 5.0 s = 20 x 0.25 s would require twenty prior 0.25 s casts (E or R only), impossible with E on 15 s and R on 80 s.

as_a_cooldown_wait_at_level_18_ranks_Q5_.Q: 7.0 s base (affectedByCdr false); with R's own sourced passive haste of 30 at rank 3: 7 x 100/(100+30) = 5.3846 s
as_a_cooldown_wait_at_level_18_ranks_Q5_.conclusion: None equals 5.0 s. The nearest candidate, the Dark Sphere recast, is 5.3846 s (or 7.0 s if R's passive haste is not applied) - not 5.0 s.

coincidences_checked_and_rejected: 8 s (W rank 5) x 100/160 = 5.0 s requires exactly 60 ABILITY HASTE - i.e. it only works if the trailing '60' in the scenario id means haste, which nothing in the cached data supports and which would leave 'custom_order' doing no work (a greedy W recast at 5.0 s is what the default order already produces).
7 s (Q) x 100/140 = 5.0 s requires exactly 40 ability haste - same objection.

W's sourced 5-second hold duration ('holds the target near her for 5 seconds') is a buff window, not a cast epoch; the audit confirms Syndra is modeled with one cast slot per ability (all five slots modeled), so there is no separate W-recast cast entry that could legitimately sit at +5.0 s.

independent_computation.step_6_result: cast_timeline[4].time = 0.25 s. Old 5.0 s is a cooldown wait that no sourced Syndra cooldown produces at this scenario's configuration, and it contradicts the charge-stocked Dark Sphere the 60-Splinter setting enables.

confidence: moderate-high on the arithmetic, moderate on the scenario reading
caveats: The scenario definition itself lives outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/golden_snapshot.py), so the exact custom cast_order and option values were inferred from the scenario id plus the cached Syndra data. The inference rests on '60' being the splinters option (a Syndra-specific sourced threshold that the module is documented to expose) rather than an ability-haste value.

Under the alternative reading '60 = 60 ability haste with no stocked charges', 5.0 s would be exactly W's rank-5 effective cooldown (8 x 100/160) and the OLD value would be correct. That reading was rejected because it makes the 'custom_order' half of the scenario id inert and because no cached Syndra source ties the number 60 to ability haste, whereas 60 is a literal Splinter-of-Wrath threshold in the cached W text.

0.25 s is a sourced constant (E and R castTime) and is a reachable epoch under the documented shared-timeline model; 5.0 s is not reachable from cast times at all and is not equal to any sourced Syndra cooldown at zero external haste. That asymmetry is the load-bearing part of the verdict.
